hook: 46 in stock. Reorder next week? One mistake
hook_tts: Forty-six in stock. Reorder next week?
hook_say: One product, 46 units on the shelf, selling 6 a day. It looks like a week of breathing room. It has one mistake.

rows.label: Units sold per day
rows.say: Say your best seller moves 6 a day.
rows.tts: Say your best seller moves six a day.
rows.why: The product's average daily sales over the last 30 days.

rows.label: Units on the shelf now
rows.tts: You've got forty-six on the shelf.
rows.why: Stock on hand, with nothing on order.

rows.label: Days until you sell out (46 / 6)
rows.say: That's almost 8 days. Order next week, right?
rows.tts: That's almost eight days. Order next week, right?
rows.why: 46 units at 6 a day lasts 7.7 days.

rows.label: Supplier delivery time
rows.say: The mistake: your supplier takes 7 days.
rows.tts: The mistake? Your supplier takes seven days.
rows.why: Lead time: the days between placing an order and having the stock to sell.

rows.label: Reorder at (42 + 20% buffer)
rows.say: 6 a day for 7 days, plus 20%: reorder at 50. You have 46.
rows.tts: Six a day for seven days, plus twenty percent. Reorder at fifty. You have forty-six.
rows.why: Reorder point = daily sales x lead time x (1 + safety stock): 6 x 7 x 1.2 = 50.4. On hand is already under it.

fix.label: When to order
fix.say: So order today. Not next week.
fix.tts: So order today. Not next week.
fix.why: On hand (46) is already under the reorder point (50.4). An order placed next week lands about 14 days from now, but 46 units at 6 a day run out in 7.7 days. The calculator also sizes the order: 6 x (7 + 14 days to the next order) x 1.2 = 151.2, less 46 on hand, rounded up = 106 units at $2.60 each, $275.60.

post.short_title: 46 in stock, reorder next week? One mistake #Shorts
post.description:
https://proofnotfluff-a11y.github.io/Proofnotfluff-pins/go/free-inventory-reorder-point-calculator/
Free reorder point calculator for online sellers: type daily sales and supplier lead time, and it shows the stock level to reorder at and how many units to order.
46 units selling 6 a day looks like 7.7 days of stock. But the supplier takes 7 days, so waiting a week means selling out before the order lands. With a 20% safety buffer the reorder point is 50.4 units (6 x 7 x 1.2), so the order is due today: enough for 3 weeks plus the buffer (151.2 units) less the 46 on hand, rounded up to 106 units at $2.60 each, $275.60. Example numbers from the free calculator's sample product. A planning estimate, not advice.

#Shorts
